newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka customs seize rare tortoises.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka customs seize rare tortoises.

text.p: Sri Lankan customs officials said on Wednesday they had seized 41 rare tortoises being smuggled to Germany.

The star tortoises, each valued between $500 and $1,000, were part of a consignment that had been declared as containing ornamental fish and plants and were seized at Colombo's international airport on Monday, customs officials told Reuters.
The star tortoises have been listed as an endangered species and are protected under Sri Lankan law.
Customs officials said they believed the consignment was part of a large-scale smuggling ring run by a German national who was using locals to smuggle endangered species out of the country.
They said Sri Lanka had also become a popular transit point in global trafficking of endangered species because of the absence of laws to punish offenders.

Large number of exotic birds, butterflies, bird's nests, live cocoons, jackal heads, animal skins and turtle shells pass through Sri Lanka daily, originating from countries such as India and Pakistan, they said.
In January, authorities fined a Danish national after he tried to smuggle 24 live tarantulas.
In June, customs officials confiscated four rare macaws which a local wildlife trader tried to bring into the country without a valid permit.

While Sri Lankan law does not allow for the seizure of endangered species which are in transit, it does provide for the confiscation of similar items brought in or taken out of the country without a proper permit.
The person who attempted to smuggle out the tortoises had been fined 100,000 rupees ($1,700) and the tortoises were handed over to Sri Lanka's Zoological Gardens Department, the officials added.
